kind: NeuroTranslation file inventory and study index
historical_sources: The portable interface source keeps the wording of the draft it was written for; it is source only and contains no model weights. Earlier paper editions and source snapshots are in the repository history.
scope: One row for every file in the repository except this record. The blocks after the rows repeat the main files of each study with their sizes and hashes.
launcher_update: The desktop shortcuts open the palm replay. The app also includes sample inspection and alignment.
base_public_commit_scope: The commit the first version of this record was made from. It is not the current head; previous_public_commit names the commit the rows were last compared with.

paper_content.scope: The current paper edition. Each new edition replaces these files in place; earlier editions are in the repository history.

download_bundle.scope: The four PDFs, the reading index (README.md and index.html), NOTICE.md, the file manifest, font provenance, the two font licence texts, the long training run's result file and the seven small result files under results/.

context_overlay_basis.meaning: An earlier commit and its tree, read as input to this record. This file does not claim that anything was committed or uploaded.

selected_source.scope: The complete source of the four PDFs (91 files: TeX, bibliography, figure, fonts and tools), the build script, and the ledger and small result files its number check reads. The TeX engine and its package files are named in the ZIP, not included.

latest_contact_force_preview.scope: Two offline grip-force forecasts compared after the tenth consecutive sample at or above 0.5 N on the 500 Hz recording clock. Adding aligned scalp EEG increased average error in both families on the same development group, which had been looked at before. The final test group is still unopened. The launchers use invented input by default.

browser.scope: Fixed ridge and causal CNN weights run on the same prior window. An invented example or compatible local JSON supplies inputs. A future target sample can be shown only when supplied. Rotation is an aggregate control. The 120 ms horizon is on the recording clock.

hygrip_force.status: Finished. The three development participants were first scored after the protocol was published; the results are in latest_hygrip_results_preview. The final test group is still unopened.
hygrip_force.scope: Cued right-hand power grip in a separate dataset. Target is a transducer-voltage reading 120 ms ahead on the released clock.

prospective_studies_note: The one study entered here when it was planned. It now has results; see latest_hygrip_results_preview.

browser.trial_replay: One right-hand trial per local file; 205 scheduled cutoffs, conditional on complete input and target support. The example is invented.
browser.signal_plot: Twenty 50 Hz transducer readings and a selectable forecast at +120 ms. Trial outcomes are shown only when revealed.

latest_hygrip_results_preview.scope: First scoring of three original HYGRIP development participants after public protocol posting. The browser uses fixed fits from the training group and invented example inputs by default. The final test group is still unopened.

secondary_emg.tested_endpoint: forecast of released sensor voltage 120 ms after issue
secondary_emg.scope: Secondary right-hand analysis on the same three previously studied development people. Timing-specific forearm EMG and scalp EEG directional screens failed on the training group and on the development group.

hygrip_cue_phase.scope: Comparison of cue-conditioned and shared voltage dynamics on the previously studied healthy HYGRIP cohort.
hygrip_cue_phase.outcome: The phase-conditioned residual did not beat the original full-history benchmark on either split. Previously studied development cohort. The full-history ridge stays the chosen model.

study.scope: Index-finger sensor voltage on a distinct two-day isometric task. Physical real-time lead remains unverified.
study.decision: Aligned EMG gave no average gain on the main measure in this experiment; results for each held-out participant and each day are reported.

latest_hyser_release.scope: Released index transducer voltage 120 ms ahead on the nominal stream. Four final participants reserved. No online or clinical claim.

crossday_study.scope: Matched Day 1 supervised calibration on an output offset and gain, followed by fixed Day 2 scoring. Shared model had the lowest mean Day 2 MAE on the four development participants, who had been studied before. Paired-donor control and pair-level descriptive uncertainty are reported.

latest_hyser_release.personal_reader: Two original same-person session folders, five labeled first-day trials, fixed second-day inference. Population mode remains available.

whole_hand.scope: Five force sensors, four prespecified fits including one other-trial control, and three same-trial predictors. MAE favored different models in the 12-person training comparison and four previously studied development participants. Reserved final participants remain unopened.

prescribed_task.scope: Unchanged Random-task weights scored on 360 prescribed N-DoF trials in 12 original fit participants and 120 in four previously evaluated development participants. Across all combinations, persistence gave lowest MAE and five histories lowest RMSE in each group. No refits. Original final participants remain excluded.

hyser_crossday.scope: Matched Day 1 supervised calibration on an output offset and gain, followed by fixed Day 2 scoring. Shared model had the lowest mean Day 2 MAE on the four development participants, who had been studied before. Paired-donor control and pair-level descriptive uncertainty are reported.

hyser_whole_hand.scope: Five force sensors, four prespecified fits including one other-trial control, and three same-trial predictors. MAE favored different models in the 12-person training comparison and four previously studied development participants. Reserved final participants remain unopened.

hyser_prescribed_task.scope: Unchanged Random-task weights scored on 360 prescribed N-DoF trials in 12 original fit participants and 120 in four previously evaluated development participants. Across all combinations, persistence gave lowest MAE and five histories lowest RMSE in each group. No refits. Original final participants remain excluded.

cemhsey_pinch.scope: Offline normalized scalar P200 pinch-force recording. Three fit participants over two days, four different evaluation participants on different indexed days. The public reader includes an invented model and supports local fit import; the study fit stays private. No cross-device physical availability or individual finger force inference.

cemhsey_array_reader.publication_scope: The public example includes invented signals and fitted example weights. A compatible locally supplied recording and locally supplied weights can be loaded in the browser.
cemhsey_array_reader.local_band_profile: Import a calibration profile bound to these weights or fit one from separate local packets.

cemhsey_interval_design.status: Measured comparison of pooled and cue-phase widths on held-out trials; the public single-trial example uses invented values.

cemhsey_force_transfer.status: Second-repeat evaluation independently reproduced across three targets.
cemhsey_force_transfer.limitations: Four previously studied adults, one indexed day, fixed repeat order and nominal timing; public examples and bundled weights are invented.

cemhsey_day_transfer.status: Second repeats on the next indexed day, scored independently; the set of source recordings was checked.
cemhsey_day_transfer.limitations: One pair of indexed days, four previously studied participants, one prescribed task and nominal 120 ms timing. Public reader uses invented signals and weights by default.

cemhsey_population_phase.status: Six test records scored on an independent group, then independently reproduced. Public ranges rounded outward under the reporting rule set before the results were seen.
cemhsey_population_phase.limitations: Three fitting and three separate evaluation participants; one target on one indexed day. Other records from these people were known in prior studies. Forecast horizon uses nominal indices.

regional_firing_in_shared_model.scope: Three training and three previously assessed test rats. Correctly aligned firing beat both controls in one test animal. Actual recorded sequence inputs to a fixed movement encoder and a separate fitted firing readout.

shared_regional_firing_browser.scope: Two fitted model families on the same recorded trip. CA1 and prefrontal firing enters the shared model at its readout after movement attention. Earlier trip firing, all three test rats, and a scrambled encoder comparison accompany the measured outcome.

knee_motion.scope: Retrospective bilateral knee angles 15 stored frames ahead at 0.5 m/s. Six Xsens HD recordings (including test S48) and 45 Live-labelled recordings. Physical prediction latency unmeasured. A four-second stride replay averaged 3.54° against 4.46° for the transformer on the same 40,201 windows. Inputs and targets were reconstructed joint angles.

gait_rhythm.scope: Separate 40-second windows in muscle and inertial joint-angle recordings from 11 held-out walkers at 0.5 m/s. Same-walk peak-frequency estimates differed by 0.027 cycles/min on average. Another walker’s muscle recording gave 3.055 cycles/min. A shared origin, event latency, gait phase and physiological step-count precision remain unverified.

walking_rhythm_supplement.scope: Five-page walking supplement covering the original and external knee forecasts, comparison with walking rhythm, and bilateral turning moments on the independent optical source.

four_second_knee_forecast.comparison: At 0.5 m/s, on the same four-second knee histories of 12 previously studied walkers, the specialist won for all 12 against replay and linear correction. Frozen weights from earlier movement tasks showed no average benefit over their scrambled control. The outcomes are stored angles.
four_second_knee_forecast.external_comparison: Frozen task-trained Transformer on ten independent optical walks at nominal 0.8 m/s. Mean absolute error 3.242 degrees against 3.398 for stride replay and 3.602 for ridge. Beat stride replay in six walkers and ridge in nine. Only the ridge comparison passed.

cortical_glove_pilot.scope: One participant, retrospective, later trials within a development prefix; surface recording did not improve the outcome over motion plus cue. Five measured glove sensors, not calibrated joint angles.

finger_motion_decoder.scope: One person, 52 earlier fitting trials and 23 later evaluation trials. Six cue/cortex models estimate five unsigned glove-sensor movement magnitudes. Adding cortex increased error for both families. Ten disjoint pairs of repeated cues did not establish a within-cue advantage.

calibrated_finger_transfer.scope: Five development participants performed a finger task. Four contributed training trials in each fold. The fifth contributed an 80-second calibration and later evaluation trials. The cue and its timing predicted the movement target better on average than the aligned Transformer.

optical_knee_moment.scope: At 0.8 m/s on a level treadmill, 400 sagittal angle frames forecast signed inverse-dynamics knee moments at t+25. Seven walkers supplied the fit, three the test moments. A task-trained model led the average among angle-only methods; its advantage varied by walker. Knowing past moments made a stronger stride-replay comparison possible.
